:::{#thm-best-predictor}
#### Conditional mean minimizes squared-error risk

Let $X$ and $Y$ be jointly distributed random variables with $\E{Y^2} < \infty$.
Let $g^*(X) \eqdef \E{Y \mid X}$.
Then for any prediction function $g(X)$ with $\E{g(X)^2} < \infty$:

$$\popriskf{g} \ge \popriskf{g^*}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.
That is, the conditional expectation function $\E{Y \mid X}$
minimizes the [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk) among all prediction functions of $X$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-risk-decomposition:

$$
\ba
\popriskf{g} - \popriskf{g^*}
&= \E{\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}}
&& \text{(@thm-risk-decomposition)} \\
&\ge 0
&& \text{(the expectation of a non-negative variable)}
\ea
$$

The expectation of the non-negative variable $\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}$ is zero
if and only if the variable is $0$ with probability $1$,
meaning $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-best-predictor}
#### The best predictor in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has risk $\popriskf{g_1} = 5$,
which is larger than the risk $\popriskf{g^*} = 1$ of the conditional mean,
and strictly so because $g_1(X) \ne g^*(X)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-irreducible-risk}
#### Irreducible risk

In the squared-error risk decomposition of @thm-risk-decomposition,
the minimum risk

$$\E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} = \E{\Var{Y \mid X}}$$

is the **irreducible risk**.

:::

::: {#rem-irreducible-risk}
#### The irreducible risk does not depend on the prediction function

The irreducible risk depends only on the joint distribution of $(X, Y)$
and not on the prediction function $g$,
so no choice of $g$ can achieve a smaller risk.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-irreducible-risk}
#### Irreducible risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
$\Var{Y \mid X = 0} = 1$ and $\Var{Y \mid X = 1} = 1$,
so the irreducible risk is $\E{\Var{Y \mid X}} = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk

In the squared-error risk decomposition of @thm-risk-decomposition,
the excess risk from choosing the prediction function $g$ instead of the conditional mean,

$$\E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}} \ge 0$$

is the **reducible risk**.

:::

::: {#rem-reducible-risk}
#### When the reducible risk is zero

The reducible risk is zero if and only if $\P(g(X) = \E{Y \mid X}) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has reducible risk $5 - 1 = 4$,
and the prediction $g_2(X) = 4X$ has reducible risk $2 - 1 = 1$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This characterization of the best predictor under squared error loss follows @hastie2009elements [Section 2.4, eq. 2.11].
The risk identity in @thm-risk-decomposition

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} = \E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} + \E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}}$$

shows that the total squared-error risk is the sum of the
irreducible risk (@def-irreducible-risk)
and the reducible risk (@def-reducible-risk).

:::
